title: Rewind Controller: cost-signature-driven config undo with prefix-quarantine for KV/batching
creator: Evan Cho
description:
Problem: Config changes that affect batching and KV cache behavior can cause rapid cost regressions (higher per-token compute, increased GPU occupancy) or latency regressions that are not always detectable by simple error-rate thresholds. We need an automated controller that can (1) detect economically harmful config changes quickly, (2) quarantine newly-introduced KV/batch artifacts to limit blast radius, and (3) perform a safe, reversible rewind (rollback) when telemetry shows sustained cost/latency regressions.

Scope: Implement a 'Rewind Controller' service that runs alongside the existing deployment orchestration. It will: compute a lightweight cost-signature for each config change, run a shadow-apply simulation for batching/cache effects, quarantine keyspaces populated under the new config (prefix-quarantine), monitor a composite rollback score, and when thresholds are exceeded, initiate a reversible rewind playbook with optional manual approval windows.

Design Summary: 
- Cost signature: for each config patch we compute a vector of normalized metrics: delta_tokens_per_request, delta_mean_latency_ms, delta_99_latency_ms, delta_gpu_token_seconds, delta_cache_hit_rate. These are normalized against baseline percentiles from the last 72h and combined into a single scalar 'cost impact score' using tunable weights.
- Shadow-apply + autosim: Before full apply, the controller will run the change in 'shadow' mode for a configurable sample (default 1% of traffic) where requests are forked and executed under the new config in an isolated path (no effects on production state). Autosim will reproduce batching/caching characteristics over rolling windows to estimate steady-state cost impact.
- Prefix-quarantine (KV cache quarantine): Any KV cache entries created while the change is in canary/shadow mode are tagged with a change id and quarantine TTL. Quarantined entries are used by the shadow path but hidden from global cache population until the change stabilizes. Quarantine reduces noisy cache pollution and provides an easy rollback path (evict quarantined keys on rewind).
- Rewind policy & decision engine: The controller computes a rolling "rollback score" combining cost signature, shadow-sim delta, and SLO regressions (error rates, tail latency). Thresholds have hysteresis and decay to prevent churning. When score > orchestrator_threshold (default 0.85) for configured_window (default 15m), controller can either auto-rewind or create an actionable rollback runbook depending on policy (auto vs manual).
- Reversible deltas: Every config apply produces a compact delta snapshot (git-style patch + metadata) stored in the config index. Rewind applies the inverse delta to restore previous state atomically; if atomic revert is not possible the controller coordinates a staged rollback with traffic shifts and staged cache evictions.
- Observability & audit: All decisions, raw signals and scoreboard history are logged to the Console. Rollback runbooks include root-cause hints (top contributing metrics and sample traces), a link to the shadow-sim artifact, and automated PR/incident links for postmortem.

APIs & Operator UX: 
- New endpoint: POST /v1/controller/preview-apply -> returns cost-signature and shadow-sim summary for a config diff.
- New endpoint: POST /v1/controller/commit-apply -> start canary apply with quarantine id and optional manual-approval window.
- Console: per-change timeline with cost-score, quarantine keycount, and 'rewind score' sparkline; one-click 'force-rewind' for admins.

Safety considerations and failure modes: 
- False positives: tune weights and use decay/hysteresis; initial rollout on non-critical customers only. 
- Shadow-sim drift: ensure sampled traffic is representative; surface population variance. 
- Partial revert failure: if reverse delta fails, controller will fallback to staged traffic shift + manual ops runbook.

Rollout plan: 
1) Prototype: implement cost-signature calculation + offline simulator (2 weeks)
2) Shadow-sim integration + quarantine tagging on testbed clusters (3 weeks)
3) Pilot: enable on 5 internal services (customer-sim workloads) with manual approval mode (4 weeks)
4) Auto-rewind opt-in for low-risk tenants + monitoring alert tuning (3 weeks)
5) Wider rollout + guardrail hardening (QA + security review)

Telemetry & success metrics: 
- Detection latency: time from first deviation to rollback decision < 10 minutes (goal < 5m).
- Cost recovery: median cost-per-token reduced back to baseline within 60 minutes after rewind.
- False positive auto-rewinds: < 2% during pilot.
- Customer-visible SLO impact reduction: 90% of rewinds prevent >5% customer-visible latency regressions.

Open questions: 
- Which weights yield the best precision/recall for rollback scoring? (need A/B trials)
- Quarantine memory overhead: eviction policies for quarantined keyspace.
- Compliance: auditing requirements for auto-rewind on enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Cost-signature produced for any config diff with documented vector fields
Shadow-sim can produce a 30m steady-state estimate for batching/cache impact from a 1% traffic sample
Prefix-quarantine tagging is persisted and quarantined keys are evictable on rewind
Controller exposes preview-apply and commit-apply endpoints and logs decisions to Console
Pilot on 5 internal services with manual-mode rewinds completed and FP rate < 2%
Automated reversible delta restore succeeds for simulated failure scenarios in staging
